status: Descriptive statistics only; no support judgments or masking runs.

mathematics.necessity: A supplied conversion factor converts the IHL word count into bytes so header and total lengths use matching units.
Subtracting header bytes from total bytes isolates the payload rather than incorrectly treating the whole packet as payload.

mathematics.key_fact: Percentage as part divided by whole
mathematics.necessity: Dividing payload bytes by total packet bytes and multiplying by 100 gives the requested percentage, unlike dividing by header bytes.
Subtracting the IHL values and multiplying by the supplied word size converts the change into bytes rather than treating the raw difference as bytes.
Multiplying the per-packet byte increase by one million gives the aggregate additional volume.
Dividing byte totals by 1,000,000 expresses transmission volumes in the specified billing unit.

financial.necessity: The stated billing scope includes headers as well as payload, so additional header bytes increase the charge.
Multiplying billed megabytes by $0.02 determines the charge without additional fees or pricing tiers.
The requested increase is the new charge minus the original charge, not the new total charge alone.

mathematics.necessity: Subtracting each batch's header size from packet length gives the payload size required by the billing clause.
Multiplying each batch's per-packet payload by its packet count and summing yields total billable bytes.
Dividing total bytes by one billion expresses usage in the decimal GB units specified for pricing.

financial.necessity: The first billable GB costs $10, while only usage above that threshold receives the $5-per-GB rate.
Fractional GB usage must be charged proportionally rather than rounded up to a whole billing unit.
The invoice must apply rates to the contractually billable quantity, linking payload calculations to payment rather than charging total packet traffic.

legal.necessity: The signed addendum's explicit override makes its billing terms control over the standard whole-packet provision.
The payload-only clause defines which transmitted bytes qualify for payment and excludes headers from billable usage.
The no-other-charges term limits the payable amount to the specified usage charges without additional fees.
